evidence.claim: Cintas describes its Uniform Rental and Facility Services segment as including rental and servicing of uniforms and other garments, mats, mops, shop towels, restroom supplies, and other rental services.

Vestis investor materials describe the company as a provider of uniform rentals and workplace supplies across the U.S. and Canada, including towels, aprons, floor care mats, linen services, managed restroom supplies, first aid and safety products, and specialty garment processing.

Vestis 2025 annual report states that the company serves more than 300,000 customer accounts and leverages supply chain, delivery fleet, and route logistics capabilities to serve customers on a recurring, typically weekly, basis.

UniFirst describes itself as one of North America’s largest uniform rental and facility service companies, providing uniforms, protective clothing, corporate image apparel, and facility service programs to diverse industries.

ABM’s public industry pages include hospitality among industries served, supporting it as a facility-services context candidate even though it was not selected into the four-candidate final list due to dilution across many verticals.

memory_update.text: Vestis is the highest-priority underfollowed candidate for the hospitality facility services and linen node because its services directly include uniforms, towels, aprons, mats, linen services, restroom supplies, first aid/safety, and route-based recurring delivery.

UniFirst should remain in the universe as a scaled but less obvious uniform rental and facility-services peer to Cintas; key gating item is customer vertical disclosure and whether hospitality/restaurant exposure is large enough to matter.

Tennant is an adjacent chokepoint candidate rather than a direct linen/uniform provider; its relevance depends on hospitality, retail, leisure, and contract-cleaner demand for labor-saving cleaning equipment and service plans.

The strongest Serenity variables for this node are route density, recurring service frequency, customer retention/churn, plant utilization, energy/water/labor costs, replacement inventory costs, and cross-sell into mats, restroom supplies, first aid, and safety products.

Most available public evidence supports service capability and business-model fit, but not precise hospitality/restaurant revenue concentration. Later layers must verify end-market mix before upgrading theme exposure.

node: Hospitality facility services, linen, uniforms, cleaning, laundry, and maintenance networks
summary: Expanded the node around route-based uniform/linen/facility services and adjacent hospitality cleaning infrastructure. Reference context is Cintas as the obvious scaled leader. Underfollowed discovery lane emphasizes Vestis, UniFirst, ABM, and Tennant: companies mapped by the market as business services, industrial services, or equipment rather than as second-order consumer travel, restaurant, lodging, and facility-utilization beneficiaries. Evidence strength is best for business-model fit; exact hospitality/restaurant revenue exposure remains a key verification gap.
